title: Bram and the Orbit
premise: Noor Reyes, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, runs supply routes between worlds that severed contact generations ago. When gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds, Noor realizes the anomaly is a message—someone at the dead relay is broadcasting an inheritance: the memory archive of the system's founders, including proof of why the worlds stopped speaking. Racing a rival salvage crew and their own failing ship, Noor must reach the relay before the signal decays forever. In the end, Noor chooses to broadcast the founders' memories to every world at once, stitching the fractured system back into a single, reluctant family.
about_author: Yara Underhill is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations in the Arctic and Andes, writing stories about people who keep things alive where nothing should grow. They now live in a coastal town with too many houseplants and one very opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet them mid-haul between two silent worlds, tending the orbital garden and trading small kindnesses with isolated outposts that pretend not to know each other. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness disguised as routine—and the first hint that Noor likes it that way.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; cargo drifts, the garden nearly dies, and every comm channel erupts with panicked chatter from worlds that supposedly can't speak to each other. Noor realizes everyone heard the same countdown tone buried in the flicker. Beat: dread blooming into curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with flashbacks to their mentor Ilsa. Examining the garden's bio-sensors, Noor finds the plants recorded the nine seconds as a pattern—a compressed signal keyed to founder-era code Ilsa once taught them. Beat: grief and inheritance intertwining; Noor understands they were left a key without being told.

chapters.title: The Salvage Crew
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Dax Okonkwo, captain of a rival salvage ship, who decoded the same pattern and intends to sell the relay's contents to the highest-bidding world. Through Dax we see the system's fractures up close: debts, embargoes, old wars. Beat: a worthy antagonist who isn't wrong about everything.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor plots a course through dead space—the radiation-shrouded corridor no ship has crossed since the Silence—to reach the edge relay. An old friend, pilot Sefa, insists on coming, forming the story's found-family core. Beat: fear met with chosen companionship.

chapters.title: The Toll
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Mid-crossing, the ship's shielding fails and they lose their fuel reserve shielding the garden module rather than themselves—an act that defines what Noor values. Sefa patches the hull while Noor confesses they've never told anyone why they tend a garden for the unborn. Beat: vulnerability as strength.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. The salvage crew reaches the relay first but finds the archive degrading faster than expected—it was never meant to last this long. Dax begins extracting only the profitable fragments, discarding the rest, and feels the first crack of doubt. Beat: ambition curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor arrives to find Dax's crew stripping the relay; a tense standoff becomes an uneasy alliance when the archive's final layer activates—the founders' own voices explaining the Silence was a cover-up of a failed terraforming war. Beat: revelation reframing everything Noor believed.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. With the relay dying, Noor and Dax must choose: sell the truth piecemeal or give it away whole. Noor reroutes the garden's transmitter array—every world's terraforming grid still listens to gardens—and broadcasts the full archive. Dax chooses, at the last second, not to stop them. Beat: sacrifice and grace under collapse.

chapters.title: First Light on New Soil
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue-like. Weeks later, replies arrive from worlds that haven't spoken in generations—angry, grieving, but speaking. The garden receives its first request for seed stock from settlers who now know the whole truth. Noor, no longer invisible, plants anyway. Beat: quiet hope; family chosen by a whole system.
